title: Galileo and Terrestrial Acceleration
description: This concept covers Galileo's groundbreaking recognition that all objects accelerate towards Earth with a constant acceleration regardless of their mass.

title: Evolution of Planetary Models
description: This concept explores the historical progression from geocentric models, like Ptolemy's, to heliocentric models proposed by Aryabhatta and Copernicus, which Galileo supported.

title: Kepler's Laws from Astronomical Data
description: This concept details how Tycho Brahe's meticulous planetary observations enabled Johannes Kepler to formulate his three laws of planetary motion.

title: Ellipse Construction Method
description: Describes how to draw an ellipse using the string and pin method, resulting in a closed curve.

title: Ellipse Foci and Constant Sum Property
description: Defines the foci of an ellipse and the fundamental property that the sum of distances from foci to any point on the ellipse is constant.

title: Ellipse Geometric Elements
description: Explains key geometric features of an ellipse, including its center and semi-major axis.

title: Circle as a Special Ellipse
description: Illustrates how a circle is a specific case of an ellipse where the two foci merge into one point.

title: Empirical Basis for Inverse Square Gravity
description: This concept explains how the centripetal acceleration of the moon and terrestrial gravity 'g' provide observational evidence for the inverse square dependence of gravitational force.

title: Newton's Universal Law: Scalar Formulation
description: This concept defines Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation, stating that the attractive force between two point masses is directly proportional to their product and inversely proportional to the square of their distance.

title: Vector Form and Newton's Third Law for Gravity
description: This concept details the vector representation of the gravitational force, emphasizing its attractive nature and its adherence to Newton's third law of action-reaction.

title: Gravitational Force with Extended Objects
description: This concept addresses how to calculate the gravitational force between extended objects, explaining the need for vector summation of forces from all constituent point masses.

title: Purpose of the Cavendish Experiment
description: This concept covers the primary objective of the Cavendish experiment, which is to experimentally determine the value of the gravitational constant G.

title: Cavendish Torsion Balance Apparatus
description: This concept describes the experimental setup consisting of a suspended bar with small spheres and nearby large spheres.

title: Torque Equilibrium in Cavendish Experiment
description: This concept explains how the gravitational torque generated by the masses is balanced by the restoring torque of the twisted suspension wire at equilibrium.

title: Deriving G from Twist Angle
description: This concept details how the gravitational constant G can be calculated by relating the angle of twist to the known experimental parameters and physical constants.

title: Gravity outside a spherical mass
description: Explains that a spherical body exerts gravitational force on an external point as if its entire mass is concentrated at its center.

title: Gravity inside a uniform sphere
description: Describes that at a point inside a uniform spherical mass, only the mass within the sphere of that radius contributes to the gravitational force.

title: Defining 'g' at Earth's surface
description: Defines the acceleration due to gravity 'g' at the Earth's surface and derives its formula using G, Earth's mass, and Earth's radius.

title: Estimating Earth's total mass
description: Explains how measuring 'g', 'G', and Earth's radius enables the calculation of the Earth's total mass.

title: Gravity above Earth's surface
description: This concept explains how the acceleration due to gravity changes with height above the Earth's surface, including a general formula and a small-height approximation.

title: Gravity below Earth's surface
description: This concept explains how the acceleration due to gravity changes with depth below the Earth's surface, deriving a linear relationship.

title: Maximum gravity at Earth's surface
description: This concept states that the acceleration due to gravity is maximum on the Earth's surface and decreases whether one goes up or down.

title: Potential Energy and Conservative Forces
description: This concept defines potential energy, relates its change to work done by forces, and introduces conservative forces, identifying gravity as one.

title: Gravitational Potential Energy Near Earth's Surface
description: This concept explains how to calculate gravitational potential energy for objects close to the Earth's surface where the gravitational force is considered constant (mg).

title: General Gravitational Potential Energy
description: This concept derives the general formula for gravitational potential energy between two masses, accounting for varying force with distance and conventionally setting potential energy at infinity to zero.

title: Gravitational Potential and Multi-Particle Systems
description: This concept defines gravitational potential as potential energy per unit mass and explains how to calculate total potential energy for systems of multiple particles using superposition.

title: Definition of Escape Speed
description: Escape speed is the minimum initial velocity an object needs to completely overcome a celestial body's gravitational pull and never fall back.

title: Applying Energy Conservation for Escape
description: The principle of conservation of energy is used to determine the initial speed required for an object to reach an infinite distance from a gravitational source.

title: Calculating Escape Speed from Surface
description: Escape speed can be calculated using the gravitational constant, mass, and radius of the celestial body, or simplified using surface gravity.

title: Factors Influencing Escape Speed and Effects
description: Escape speed depends on a body's mass and radius, with lower values for smaller, less massive bodies explaining phenomena like the Moon's lack of atmosphere.

title: Forces in Satellite Circular Orbit
description: This concept explains how the centripetal force required for a satellite's circular motion is provided by the gravitational force between the Earth and the satellite.

title: Calculating Satellite Orbital Speed
description: This concept shows how to derive the satellite's speed in a circular orbit by equating the gravitational force to the centripetal force.

title: Satellite Orbital Period and Kepler's Third Law
description: This concept explains how to calculate the time period of a satellite's circular orbit and demonstrates its relationship to the orbital radius, confirming Kepler's Law of Periods.

title: Kinetic Energy of Orbiting Satellites
description: This concept covers how to determine the kinetic energy of a satellite moving in an orbit.

title: Gravitational Potential Energy of Orbiting Satellites
description: This concept explains how to calculate the gravitational potential energy of an orbiting satellite, typically with zero potential energy at infinity.

title: Total Energy and KE/PE Relationship in Circular Orbits
description: This concept details the fixed relationship between kinetic, potential, and total energy for a satellite in a circular orbit, including their signs and magnitudes.

title: Total Energy in Elliptic Orbits
description: This concept describes how kinetic and potential energies vary in elliptic orbits while the total energy remains constant and negative.

title: Total Energy Sign and Orbital Boundness
description: This concept explains that negative total energy signifies a bound orbit, while positive or zero total energy indicates escape from gravitational influence.
